category_title: Honors students experiencing anxiety with higher-order analytical tasks
minimal_context: The student is transitioning from reading about qualitative methods to coding and analyzing their collected field notes for their honors project.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Now that the research deadlines are nearing, it is time to move from the assigned readings to actually coding and analyzing your field notes.

STUDENT: I was really optimistic about my abilities to successfully engage in the research process early on. But now that we actually have to do it, I'm starting to question my abilities, despite the fact that I have previously taken another research methods class.

TUTOR: Just try to process the information and find patterns in your data.

STUDENT: It is much easier to regurgitate information than to process it, try to find patterns, make sense of it, and see it applied in the larger picture. I'm surprised at my feelings of frustration and inadequacy given the relative ease I've experienced in my other honors courses.

TUTOR: Go ahead and start coding the data you collected.

STUDENT: I'm absolutely petrified. Talking and reading about versus doing qualitative research is the same as if I read a book on 'the process of how to successfully catch an Amazon Marmoset', and then someone tossed me into the rain forest expecting me to find my way. My anticipation has melted into fear and doubt, and I can not help but think I am way out of my league.

options.A: Use a structured questioning route that moves from opening observations to identifying problems and exploring alternative non-defensive behaviors.
options.B: Request that the student hold all questions about coding and analyzing field notes until the end of the seminar.
options.C: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during instruction on coding and analyzing field notes.
options.D: Employ reflective journaling, asking the student to share their thoughts and emotions about the qualitative research process.
